claims.text: In \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\), Schur classes form a graded basis and multiplication is truncated Littlewood–Richardson multiplication inside \((n-r)^r\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-218]

groundings.excerpt:
213: Let $\Lambda=\Lambda(x_1,x_2,\ldots)$ be the ring of symmetric functions with integral coefficients. This space has a ${\mathbb Z}$-linear basis consisting of \emph{Schur functions} $s_{\lambda}$,
214: where $\lambda$ is an integer partition. Consider the ideal
215: \[I_{r,n-r} = \mathrm{Span}_\mathbb{Z}\left\{s_\lambda\mid \lambda\nsubseteq (n-r)^r \right\} \]
216: of $\Lambda$. Then one has the following standard presentation of the cohomology of Grassmannians:
217: \[H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})\cong \Lambda/I_{r,n-r}. \]
218: We will use an overline to denote the projection $\Lambda\to\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}$. Specifically, we will write $\overline{\Lambda}$ as a shorthand for $\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}$. We will also distinguish between $s_{\lambda}\in \Lambda$, the usual Schur function, and $\overline{s}_{\lambda}$ for its image in $\overline{\Lambda}$.

claims.text: For the accepted case \(A=\Lambda/I_{5,4}\), \(J=\bigoplus_{222\subseteq\lambda\subseteq4^5}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda\), and \(A_+=(h_1,h_2,h_3,h_4)\), the degree-\(d\) relation lattice \((A_+J)_d\) is exactly the row span of all Pieri rows \(h_t\bar s_\lambda\), \(1\le t\le4\), \(|\lambda|=d-t\), \(\lambda\in[222,4^5]\), with terms outside \(4^5\) zero.
With partition-weight grading, \(Q_d=(J/A_+J)_d\) satisfies \[ (Q_6,Q_7,Q_8,Q_9,Q_{10})\cong (\mathbb Z,\mathbb Z,\mathbb Z^2,\mathbb Z,\mathbb Z), \] without torsion.

The complete Pieri computation has unit Smith diagonals in degrees \(11,\ldots,20\), hence \(Q_d=0\) there; \(J_d=0\) outside \(6\le d\le20\). [artifact 7af8794736d117dae1e41cf900ae797f4928431403d66c0204057b898ccb954d]
Thus \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^6\). Every homogeneous generating family for \(J\) has at least two degree-\(8\) members and at least six members in total. There is no torsion obstruction in this case.
